name: shamrock

attributes.attribute: turned the shamrock to a Trinity symbol
four-leaf form used for fairy ointment

sources: Carmichael, Alexander. Carmina Gadelica: Hymns and Incantations. Hudson, N.Y.: Lindisfarne Press, 1992, pp. 155–156.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The shamrock is a symbolic plant. The clover and the wood sorrel both carry the name shamrock. No proof shows either was sacred to the Celts in early days. The Celts held a philosophy of triplicity. Their divinities often came in three. When the mission of Saint Patrick needed a homely symbol, he chose the shamrock. On Beltane he held one up before the Druids and spoke of the Trinity, the three-in-one God. He did more than find a simple image. He touched the Celtic love of the number three, and the reach of that symbol eased his work. A shamrock with a fourth leaf worked against the rule of three. People prized it for making fairy ointment, the gift that lets the eye see the hidden world.
